title: Return policy page found
question: Can an agent find and read the return policy?
method: Follow the home-page link whose label or path names returns, refunds, exchanges, withdrawal, Widerruf, Rückgabe, retour, reso or their equivalents, as whole words. A label made of policy words outranks a product name that carries the word, a footer link outranks a body link, and product, listing and account URLs are never chosen. On Shopify the platform's own policy page replaces a missing pick or one matched only weakly, such as by path alone. When the home page links no such page, a same-site sitemap URL whose last path segment names the policy document (/returns-policy, /refund-policy) is used instead; the page is still fetched and judged. Fail when no link is found, when the linked page does not answer 200 or when it is a product page rather than a policy. Skipped as inconclusive when the page refused the scanner, was challenged or rate limited, answered 502, 503 or 504, or did not answer: such an answer says nothing about the policy, so it never counts as a fail, and when it alone stands before Level 3 the level is reported as not decided rather than missed. Warn when it carries 100 words or fewer. Pass otherwise. When the home page is an empty shell that JavaScript fills in (fewer than 3 links and fewer than 50 words in its HTML), the failure message says so: the policy may exist for people, but an agent reading HTML has no link to follow. Every checkout programme (Google Merchant Center and UCP, the OpenAI feed, Stripe, Shopify channels) asks for a return policy URL.

title: Shipping policy page found
question: Can an agent find shipping costs, regions and delivery times?
method: The same link heuristics as B4.1 for shipping, delivery, Versand, Lieferung, livraison, spedizione, envío and their compounds (Versandkosten counts, Versandlager does not), with the same Shopify and sitemap fallbacks and the same message for an empty-shell home page. Fail when no link is found, when the linked page does not answer 200 or when it is a product page. Skipped as inconclusive when the page refused the scanner, was challenged or rate limited, answered 502, 503 or 504, or did not answer, as in B4.1. Warn when its text names no amount with a currency, no delivery time in days and no shipping keyword such as free shipping, Versandkosten or worldwide. Pass otherwise.

title: Privacy policy and terms found
question: Are the privacy policy and terms of service linked and fetchable?
method: Look for link labels or paths matching privacy, Datenschutz, terms, AGB, conditions, T&Cs and their equivalents, ranked as in B4.1 so that Terms of Service outranks Promo T&Cs, with the same Shopify and sitemap fallbacks and the same message for an empty-shell home page. Pass when both pages answer 200. Warn when only one does. Fail when neither does. When a page was linked but could not be read, the message names the link and the response. Skipped as inconclusive when every linked page that is not readable refused the scanner, was challenged or rate limited, answered 502, 503 or 504, or did not answer, as in B4.1.

spec.title: OpenAI product feed specification: seller_tos and seller_privacy_policy

title: Merchant identity
question: Who is selling, where are they, and how can they be reached?
method: Pass when Organization JSON-LD (or a subtype such as OnlineStore or LocalBusiness) carries a name and at least one of address, contactPoint, telephone or email. The scanner reads the home page first, then the linked imprint page, then the linked contact page. An imprint page (imprint, Impressum, legal notice, mentions légales and their equivalents) whose text shows a postal code with a place name and a street with a house number also passes. Warn when the best Organization node lacks a name or any contact detail, or when there is no Organization node and the imprint page answers without a complete postal address. Fail when there is neither.

title: Contact channel
question: Can an agent or its user find a way to contact the merchant?
method: Pass when the home page links a mailto: address, a tel: number, or a contact, support, help, FAQ or customer-service page on the store's own site or one of its subdomains (the words must stand alone in a short label or in the last path segment, and product, listing and account pages never count). Warn when only a contact link to another site exists. Fail when there is none, saying so when the home page is an empty shell that JavaScript fills in. The message names a page. Google Merchant Center requires a contact method on the site, and UCP onboarding asks for at least one.

title: Policy pages are agent-readable
question: Can an agent actually read the policy pages it found?
method: For each policy page found (returns, shipping, privacy, terms), leaving out a page that B4.1 or B4.2 rejected as a product page, require HTTP 200, more than 100 words of text outside scripts, and, on the store's own origin, no robots.txt rule that disallows, on its path, the core and major-assistant crawlers that fetch pages for an index ({{crawlers:index.core}} and the major assistants' search crawlers of A2.2; control tokens such as Google-Extended and regional services do not count). Pass when all found pages qualify. Warn when some do not, or when all qualify but a page carries noindex (reachable for every fetcher, but kept out of the indexes that ground AI answers, as Shopify policy pages are by default). Fail when none qualifies. Skip when no policy page was found.

title: security.txt
question: Does the site publish a security contact?
method: Informational. GET /.well-known/security.txt. Pass on a non-HTML document with a Contact field and an Expires date in the future. Warn when Contact is missing, Expires is missing or unreadable, or the date has passed. Not applicable when the file does not answer 200 or an HTML page answers instead. Operational maturity, not agent readiness: reported, never scored.
